messages:
Alex: Heads-up — provisioning failures in us-west1: GPU nodes are hanging at mount time. A bunch of boots show `waiting for local scratch` and never finish.
Maria: We saw a big fsync latency spike from ephemeral NVMe yesterday around 03:10 UTC. Correlates with janitor/cleanup runs.
SRE-Bot: alert: nvme_fsync_latency > 1s on us-west1-a, rate=172/min, affected_hosts=64 :warning:
Chris: logs from node-3412:
```
[ 1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[ 1234.568012] write(0x7f3) took 1250 ms, fsync blocked
```
Alex: that 1.25s fsync is killing container startup — our GPU attach logic waits on overlay fsyncs. If multiple cleaners hit same device we get a convoy.
Maria: digging into janitor schedule — last deploy bumped concurrency default from 2 -> 8 for faster reclaim. That probably amplified write bursts and competing fsyncs.
Chris: temporary mitigation: roll janitor back to concurrency=1 for us-west1 and add `--fsync-delay-ms=200` to smoother coalescing. Will push in the next 10m.
Rafael: can we also throttle the scrub process? We have a heavy background compaction on nodes with older firmware that I suspect behaves poorly under parallel fsync.
Maria: yes — plan: (1) reduce janitor concurrency (2) lower scrub parallelism (3) move affected hosts to maintenance pool so new GPU jobs go elsewhere.
Alex: how many hosts are affected? need quick list to cordon
SRE-Bot: hosts flagged: [node-3412, node-3420, node-3499, node-3501, node-3555, ...] (64 total)
Chris: I'll trigger cordon for the 64, but we'll still need ~2h for rolling janitor config rollout and validation.
Jamie: I'll open an incident doc and note customer-impacting provisioning failures. Short postmortem checklist in docs.
Rafael: longer-term: vendor reported a firmware edge-case where concurrent fsyncs can slow down NVMe controller internal write flush by orders of magnitude. We should schedule a staged firmware update and coordinate with capacity to avoid disruptions.
Alex: action items:
- Chris: apply janitor concurrency rollback + fsync coalescing in us-west1 (in progress)
- Maria: run IO latency baseline pre/post change and post here
- Rafael: draft firmware rollout plan and get vendor patch notes
- Jamie: incident doc + customer comms if SLOs degrade
Chris: started config rollout now. patch: `replicator set janitor.concurrency=1 --region=us-west1` — monitoring: dashboard nvme_fsync_latency dropping already :thumbsup:
Maria: after change, 10m baseline shows p95 fsync down from 1.2s -> 120ms. Provision success rate up from 82% -> 98% in the test cohort.
Alex: good. Keep cordon until we finish firmware plan. If p95 creeps above 300ms we fallback to routing requests to other regions.
Jamie: writing up timeline and RCA notes. tagging @support for potential customer alerts.
Rafael: will schedule a canary firmware update for 10 nodes next Tue during low-traffic window and report metrics.
Chris: leaving this thread open for next 24h, will post final remediation summary once firmware plan is green.
Jamie: noted — incident doc link: https://internal.redwood/incident/2026-03-nvme-fsync
Maria: thanks y'all, nice quick catch. :raised_hands:
Alex: closing loop once firmware canary passes. :white_check_mark:
